what_happened: The job was meant to route checks by job kind, following section 3.2 of the ci-routing design, and to change athena.toml. It was rejected. The verifier's verdict was fail, and the final verdict said the reading misread the request. Two blocker or major findings are listed. (1) Major: a docs, design or study job now skips fmt and clippy even when it changes Rust code. The design says these checks are skipped only when prose alone changed, "as today", and that verification is not weakened. The code involved is route() in crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs, the skip_for_kinds setting in athena.toml, and the checks loop in run.rs. (2) Major: the reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met. No unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks are listed.
cause: Nothing compares the accepted reading with the request or the cited design before the build starts. The design's condition ("only when prose alone changed, not weakening verification") was turned into a rule keyed on job kind alone. Nothing required the reading to carry that safety condition as a criterion, or required a test that a docs-kind job touching Rust code still runs fmt and clippy. Criteria written from the faulty reading passed, so the gap showed only at the final verdict. This is an inference, since the request text and reading are not in the stored fields.
prevention: Add a pre-build reading check. When a request cites a design section, each invariant or exclusion in that section (such as "skip only when prose alone changed" or "verification is not weakened") must map to a named acceptance criterion and a named test. The reading is not accepted until the mapping is complete. For routing, require a test showing that a docs, design or study job that changes Rust files still runs fmt and clippy. Also have the build compare the changed file types with the skip rule before handover.
proposed_request: Fix check routing from ci-routing 3.2 so that fmt and clippy are skipped only when the change is prose alone, not merely because the job kind is docs, design or study. A job of any kind that changes Rust code (any .rs file, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock) must still run fmt and clippy, so verification is not weakened. Keep the skip as it works today for prose-only changes. Update route() in crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs, the skip_for_kinds setting in athena.toml, and the checks loop in run.rs as needed, and make sure athena.toml still parses under the config schema. Acceptance: (1) a test where a docs-kind job changes only markdown skips fmt and clippy; (2) a test where a docs, design or study job changes a Rust file runs fmt and clippy; (3) a test where a code job runs all checks; (4) cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check pass, with the commands and their output recorded as evidence; (5) the change is limited to routing and its config.
